headline: BTC taps $85K, an 8-month high, on a $648M short squeeze - there is no dip here
summary: Bitcoin ran from about $81,000 to $85,057 in the last 12 hours, its highest since January, and the move was mechanical: of roughly $750m of crypto liquidations in 24h, $648.3m were shorts, $360.7m of that in BTC. The trigger was outside crypto - Brent fell a third straight day to about $101.71 (-2.08%) as traders priced hopes of a US-Iran diplomatic opening at the UN General Assembly, and equities and US futures followed oil down in risk premium. Underneath that, the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September, its first increase since 2023, and markets still price about 56% odds of another in October, so the macro backdrop is hawkish rather than supportive. Institutions leaned in again: Strategy bought 950 BTC at an average $79,670 ($75.7m) last week, its first weekly purchase since late August, and filed an 8-K this morning. Mood is Greed - composite sentiment 74.3, Fear & Greed 70 - and all three majors are up on the week (BTC +9.2%, ETH +8.6%, SOL +15.2%), so this is a chase-or-wait tape, not a panic-dip tape.

BTC.note: At $85,057 after a +5% day and +9.2% week, driven by forced short covering rather than visible spot demand, with perp funding still mild at 0.0063%/h.

ETH.note: At $2,722, +5.6% on the day and +8.6% on the week, with the lowest funding of the three majors (0.0024%/h) and ether ETFs having just snapped a four-week inflow streak.

SOL.note: At $116.79 and the strongest of the three on the week (+15.2%), but it carries the most event risk: the CLARITY Act failure and the Alpenglow mainnet activation targeted for 28 September.

drivers.title: Short squeeze carries BTC to $85,000
drivers.detail: Bitcoin briefly touched $85,000, its highest level since January, as roughly $750m of crypto positions were liquidated in 24 hours, $648.3m of them shorts (86% of the day, 96% in the final hour). ETH rose 5.6% to about $2,717 and SOL 7.2% to about $115.75 alongside it.

drivers.title: Oil risk premium deflates on US-Iran diplomacy hopes
drivers.detail: Brent fell about 2.08% to $101.71 and WTI 2.14% to $98.15, a third straight decline, as traders priced a possible diplomatic path in the US-Iran war and a partial recovery in Saudi shipments. Cheaper oil is what lifted equities and crypto together today, which means the crypto bid is borrowed from a geopolitical headline that can reverse.

drivers.title: Fed hiked on 16 September and may hike again in October
drivers.detail: The FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, its first hike since 2023, citing elevated inflation, and 16 of 18 participants see another increase possible this year. Markets price about 56% odds of an October hike with the US 2-year near 4.75%, so rates are a headwind working against today's tape.

drivers.title: Big money steps back in: Strategy buys, ETFs turn positive
drivers.detail: Strategy bought 950 BTC at an average $79,670 ($75.7m) last week, its first weekly buy since late August, taking holdings to about 846,000 BTC at an average $74,417, and filed an 8-K at 12:00 UTC today. US spot bitcoin ETFs took in $433m on 18 September (FBTC $310.7m, IBIT $108m), enough to keep the week barely positive at $6.2m net.

drivers.title: ECB puts central bank money on tokenised rails
drivers.detail: The ECB announced at 10:00 UTC that the Eurosystem is bringing central bank money to tokenised finance via its Pontes platform and will invest part of its own funds in tokenised securities - settlement that deliberately routes around stablecoins. It is structurally supportive of tokenisation but not of stablecoin issuers.

drivers.title: CLARITY Act still dead in the Senate
drivers.detail: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act failed its cloture vote 49-50 on 15 September, well short of the 60 needed, leaving US market-structure rules unresolved. That overhang weighs hardest on high-beta alts such as SOL, while the SEC's separate tokenised-stock push moves ahead without legislation.

watch.what: US S&P Global flash PMIs, the first activity read after the Fed hike; euro area flash PMIs land 08:00 UTC and the UK 08:30 UTC.
A dense run of Fed speakers now that the 17 September blackout has lifted; any hawkish tilt feeds the ~56% October hike odds already priced.
Deribit quarterly options expiry, about $14.73bn BTC open interest plus $1.92bn ETH, near $16.6bn notional - the largest single source of mechanical volatility this week.
Plasma (XPL) cliff unlock of roughly 1.76-1.81bn tokens, about 63-65% of circulating supply (~$158m) - an alt-specific supply shock that can bleed into risk appetite.
Solana Alpenglow mainnet activation target; Anza's Agave 4.3 became the general validator recommendation today, the last practical checkpoint.

UN General Assembly diplomacy on the US-Iran war and the anticipated Trump-Xi meeting after Bessent called last week's tariff and AI talks successful; both are what the oil-driven risk bid is resting on.
